title: Recording: Children Children, B Side To Seaside, London Town, Girls School by Wings | 1977
content:
Studio Three, Abbey Road Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Peter Henderson, Mark Vigars

Wings worked on four songs at Abbey Road on 18 February 1977.

They had rehearsed and settled upon an arrangement for ‘Children Children’ on 15 February. The backing track was recorded on this day, and had Paul McCartney on bass guitar, Denny Laine on autoharp, Jimmy McCulloch on acoustic guitar, and Joe English on harmonica.

Wings then attempted to record ‘B-Side To Seaside’, intended for the flipside of Linda McCartney’s Suzy And The Red Stripes single ‘Seaside Woman’. However, the song was re-recorded on 16 March 1977.

Wings also worked on overdubs for the songs ‘London Town’ and ‘Girls School’ before the end of this session.

A visitor to the session was studio engineer Geoff Emerick, who had recently worked on the Harbor album for the band America. It was recorded in Hawaii, and Emerick’s news gave Wings the idea of moving the London Town sessions to warmer climes.

This was also the final Wings recording session prior to the McCartneys’ holiday in Jamaica, which lasted from 19 February until early March.
